patients.summary: Construction laborer with HIV off therapy and opioid use disorder with heroin injection who joins the practice in August 2024. Culture-negative polyarticular septic arthritis (2024), wound botulism (2025) and tuberculous meningitis (2026, after his last practice visit) follow, with ART and buprenorphine started, lapsed and restarted.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Brandon phoned looking for a primary doctor. Says he hasn't had one in a couple of years and his old HIV clinic "dropped" him after he stopped going. Has MassHealth. Booked new-patient visit 8/20 at 9:00. Asked him to bring any pill bottles and the name of the old clinic so we can request records. Best contact is cell, ok to text.

conditions.label: Human immunodeficiency virus disease
conditions.note: diagnosed about 2019 at an outside clinic; off ART over a year

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

32M, construction laborer, here to get set up with primary care. Two things he wants on the table right away: he has HIV and he uses heroin.

HIV: told he was positive around 2019 at a clinic out of the area. Was on a once-daily pill for a while, doesn't remember the name. Stopped going more than a year ago, ran out, never refilled. No thrush, no weight loss he's noticed, no night sweats, no cough. Doesn't know his last CD4.

Opioids: injects heroin, most days, for years. Tried buprenorphine once "a long time ago," got it off the street mostly, never in a program. Denies overdose in the past year. Uses his own works most of the time, admits not always new. Knows about the syringe exchange.

PMH: as above. No surgeries. Meds: none. Allergies: none known.
FH: dad has coronary disease, mom high blood pressure, brother treated for depression.
SH: lives alone, apartment. Works construction, day labor lately. Smokes a pack a day, since about 20. Drinks a beer or two a month. Single.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: thin, pleasant, cooperative, a little guarded at first. Vitals reviewed, afebrile. No thrush, no adenopathy cervical/axillary. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Old track marks both antecubital fossae, no abscess, no cellulitis. Joints normal. Skin otherwise clear.
PHQ-9 6, AUDIT-C 1.

A/P
1. HIV, not on treatment. Viral load, CD4, hep B/C, RPR, CBC, CMP today. Referral to the HIV clinic; he agrees to go. Explained that treatment now is one pill and that undetectable means he can't pass it on.
2. Opioid use disorder, injecting. Offered to start buprenorphine here, either home start or in office. He wants to think about it, "not ready this week." Door is open. Talked about not using alone, fentanyl test strips, new needles each time.
3. Tobacco. Advised quitting. Not interested right now, declined patch/gum.
4. Prevention: hep B status pending; will vaccinate if non-immune. Flu shot when available.

RTC 2-4 weeks, sooner if he wants to start bup.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Brandon, your labs are back. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests are normal. Hepatitis C and syphilis tests are negative. The HIV viral load is 41,000 and your CD4 is 318, which tells me your immune system is still in decent shape but the virus is active, so getting back on treatment soon matters. The HIV clinic should call you this week to schedule. You are not immune to hepatitis B, so I'd like to give you that vaccine at your next visit. Call or text me with questions.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department, community teaching hospital
Patient: Brandon Crowley  DOB 06/02/1992
Date of service: 10/28/2024
PCP on file: primary care internal medicine (copy sent)

CC: fever, aching all over, joints swollen

HPI: 32-year-old man with HIV (not currently treated) and opioid use disorder who injects. About two weeks of fevers and feeling run down. Joint pain started in both knees and over the following days moved into his wrists and elbows. No injury. No recent travel. No rash noticed, no urethral discharge.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
PMH: HIV, opioid use disorder. PSH: none.
FH: father CAD, mother HTN, brother MDD.
SH: injects heroin; smokes 1 ppd; rare alcohol.

Triage: T 38.9 C (102 F), HR 110, BP 130/85.

Exam: ill-appearing, diaphoretic. Knees, wrists and elbows each warm and red, exquisitely tender, motion limited by pain; right knee with a large effusion. Heart tachycardic with a regurgitant murmur not documented before. Lungs clear. No splinter hemorrhages or conjunctival petechiae noted. Antecubital track marks, no abscess.

Results: WBC 15.0 K/uL. ESR 85 mm/hr. CRP 120 mg/L. BMP unremarkable.
Right knee arthrocentesis (bedside, sterile prep): turbid fluid. Synovial WBC 60,000/uL, 90% neutrophils. Gram stain: no organisms. No crystals. Culture sent. Blood cultures x2 drawn before antibiotics.

ED course: vancomycin and ceftriaxone IV after cultures. Acetaminophen. Orthopedics and medicine consulted.

Impression: septic arthritis, polyarticular, in a person who injects drugs; new murmur, endocarditis to be excluded.
Disposition: admitted to medicine.

medications.drug: bictegravir 50 MG / emtricitabine 200 MG / tenofovir alafenamide 25 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily

medications.drug: buprenorphine 8 MG / naloxone 2 MG Sublingual Film
medications.sig: Dissolve 1 film under the tongue twice daily
1 spray in one nostril for suspected overdose; may repeat in 2-3 minutes
Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily through 11/26/2024

reports.text: Indication: fever, new murmur, injection drug use. Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness with normal systolic function, estimated ejection fraction 60%. Right ventricle normal size and function. Aortic, mitral, tricuspid and pulmonic valves structurally normal with normal leaflet motion. No vegetation seen. No significant valvular regurgitation or stenosis. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal with normal respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: Normal study. No echocardiographic evidence of endocarditis.

documents.title: Orthopedics: right knee arthroscopic irrigation and debridement
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Orthopaedic Surgery Operative Report
Date of surgery: 10/29/2024
Preoperative diagnosis: septic arthritis, right knee (polyarticular presentation)
Postoperative diagnosis: same
Procedure: arthroscopic irrigation and debridement, right knee
Anesthesia: general
Allergies: NKDA

Findings: cloudy, thin fluid on entry. Diffuse synovitis with fibrinous debris in the suprapatellar pouch and both gutters. Articular cartilage intact. Menisci and cruciates intact.

Standard anterolateral and anteromedial portals. Fluid sampled for culture. Synovectomy of inflamed tissue with shaver; 9 L of saline lavage. Portals closed with nylon. Sterile dressing. No complications. EBL minimal.

Plan: weight bearing as tolerated, knee range of motion with PT, antibiotics per medicine/ID. Suture removal at 10-14 days.

documents.title: Discharge Summary: septic arthritis
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Community teaching hospital, Medicine Service
Admitted 10/28/2024, discharged 11/12/2024

Principal diagnosis: septic arthritis, polyarticular (knees, wrists, elbows), culture-negative
Other: HIV, off ART at admission; opioid use disorder, injection use
Allergies: NKDA

Course:
- Joints: right knee aspirate with 60,000 WBC, 90% neutrophils, no organisms on Gram stain. Arthroscopic washout of the right knee 10/29. Wrists and elbows improved on antibiotics alone. Synovial and blood cultures (2 sets) final with no growth. Vancomycin plus ceftriaxone IV for 14 days, transitioned to oral linezolid 600 mg BID for another 14 days (last dose 11/26). ESR 85 to 40 and CRP 120 to 18 mg/L by discharge.
- Murmur: heard in the ED while febrile and tachycardic, not appreciated after day 3. TTE 10/30 with normal valves, no vegetation, EF 60%. With negative cultures, felt to be a flow murmur; no endocarditis.
- HIV: VL 52,000, CD4 285. ID consulted; started bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide daily on 11/1. Follow-up booked at the HIV clinic.
- OUD: addiction consult. Buprenorphine/naloxone started, now 8/2 mg film twice daily, no withdrawal, no cravings by discharge. Naloxone nasal spray given. Bridge script to 11/26; PCP to continue.

Discharge medications:
1. bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 1 tab daily
2. buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 mg SL film BID
3. linezolid 600 mg PO BID through 11/26
4. naloxone 4 mg nasal spray PRN

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week, HIV clinic 12/11, orthopedics for suture removal.
Weekly CBC while on linezolid.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transitional care call. Home since 11/12. Taking linezolid, the HIV pill and the films; picked everything up. Knees sore but walking, wrists better. No fever. Using a cane his neighbor lent him. Booked with PCP 11/19 (sutures out at ortho 11/22). Reminded him of the weekly blood count while on linezolid; can be drawn at the visit.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit, discharge summary reviewed.

Admitted 10/28-11/12 for culture-negative septic arthritis of knees, wrists and elbows; R knee scoped and washed out. Echo normal. Now on day 7 of oral linezolid, finishes 11/26. Started HIV meds in hospital and buprenorphine.

How he's doing: fevers gone. R knee stiff in the morning, loosens after 20 min. Wrists and elbows nearly back to normal. Off the cane mostly. No diarrhea, no numbness or vision change on linezolid. Taking the HIV pill every morning with the films. No use since admission, says cravings are "way down." Has naloxone at home.

Exam: afebrile, vitals ok. Weight down 5 kg from August. R knee portals healing, small effusion, warm-ish but not hot, flexion to about 110. L knee, wrists, elbows without effusion, full motion. Heart regular, no murmur today. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Septic arthritis, improving. Finish linezolid. CBC and CRP today. PT exercises from hospital. Call for fever or new joint swelling.
2. HIV, ART restarted 11/1. HIV clinic 12/11.
3. OUD on buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 BID. I'll take over prescribing from here. PDMP checked, only the hospital bridge script. Urine screen today: buprenorphine positive, otherwise negative. Rx for 4 weeks.
4. Flu shot and PCV20 today.
5. Smoking: still a pack a day. Not ready.

RTC 4 weeks.

documents.title: CBC and CRP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood counts normal, platelets fine on the linezolid. CRP down to 9. Good. Finish the pills on the 26th.

documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Infectious Disease / HIV Clinic
Visit date: 12/11/2024
Re: Brandon Crowley

Seen in follow-up after starting bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide during his October admission. Reports taking it every morning, missed maybe two doses. Tolerating it without nausea or GI upset. Finished linezolid 11/26; joints feel fine apart from some right knee stiffness.

Meds: bictegravir/FTC/TAF daily; buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 mg BID (PCP); naloxone nasal spray.
Allergies: NKDA.

Today: HIV-1 RNA 180 copies/mL (from 52,000), CD4 344.

Assessment: good early virologic response. Expect suppression on the next check. Continue current regimen. Return in 6 months with labs, sooner if problems.

Infectious Disease attending

documents.title: Buprenorphine Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing well on 8/2 twice a day. No heroin since October. Some evening cravings on weekends, manageable. Working a few days a week again, light duty. R knee still a bit stiff going down ladders. Saw the HIV clinic last week, viral load already way down (letter in chart). Smoking unchanged.

O: vitals fine. Calm, engaged. R knee no effusion, flexion near full.
PDMP reviewed, appropriate. UDS: buprenorphine +, otherwise negative.

- Hep B vaccine #1 today, #2 in a month.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Monthly visit. Says January is slow for work which makes the days long. Still no use. Taking the HIV pill most days, "forgot a couple over New Year's." Knee is back to normal, kneeling on job sites without trouble, wrists and elbows fine.

Weight back up 3 kg. Exam: R knee no effusion, full ROM, portals healed. Wrists/elbows normal. No murmur.
UDS bup +, otherwise neg. PDMP ok.

2. OUD: continue buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 BID, 4 wk Rx. Talked about what slow weeks do to cravings and having a plan.
3. HIV: on ART, next HIV clinic visit in June. Reinforced daily dosing.
4. Hep B #2 today, series complete. MenACWY #1 today (recommended with HIV), #2 in 8+ weeks.

RTC 1 month (video ok).

On 8/2 BID. Reports more cravings the past couple weeks, a friend he used with is back in town. Denies use. Not keen on increasing the dose; we agreed he'll call if it gets worse and we could go to 8 mg three times a day. Still has naloxone. HIV meds "mostly."

documents.title: Neurology ICU consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology Consultation, Neuro ICU
Date of service: 04/19/2025
Patient: Brandon Crowley, 32M

Reason: acute cranial nerve palsies and weakness.

HPI: Two days ago his eyelids began to droop; since then he has had double vision, food and pills sticking when he swallows, and his speech has become thick. He has HIV and opioid use disorder; septic arthritis last fall. He says he had been off his buprenorphine and his HIV medication for about a month and went back to heroin, last injecting three days ago into the right forearm with a needle that was not clean.

Allergies: none known. Meds: none currently.

Exam: afebrile. BP 130/85, pulse 70, RR 16, saturating well on room air. Alert, fully oriented, follows commands. Ptosis on both sides. Pupils dilated and fixed to light. Dysarthric. Weakness is symmetric and descends from the cranial muscles. Sensation normal throughout. Reflexes present and symmetric. No rash. Right forearm with a small puncture site, no redness, fluctuance or drainage.

Labs: WBC 12,000, Hgb 14.2, plt 250,000. Na 140, K 4.2, Cr 1.0, glucose 98.

Impression: clinical picture of wound botulism from heroin injection.
Recommendations: heptavalent antitoxin now via the state health department, do not wait for confirmation. Serum for toxin assay before antitoxin. Surgical exploration and debridement of the forearm site. IV penicillin G. Vital capacity and negative inspiratory force every 4 hours; low threshold to intubate. NPO, swallow evaluation. Neurology will follow daily.

documents.title: Discharge Summary: wound botulism
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Community teaching hospital
Admitted 04/19/2025 (Neuro ICU), transferred to floor 04/27, discharged 05/07/2025

Principal diagnosis: wound botulism (right forearm injection site)
Other: HIV, off ART for ~1 month before admission; opioid use disorder, relapse
Allergies: NKDA

Course: Heptavalent botulinum antitoxin given on the day of admission. Pre-treatment serum positive for botulinum toxin type A (state laboratory). Right forearm site explored and debrided 04/20, no abscess. Penicillin G IV for 10 days. Vital capacity followed closely in the ICU, declined modestly then stabilized; never needed intubation. NG tube feeding 6 days until speech-language pathology cleared him for a regular diet. Ptosis and eye movements improved slowly; at discharge mild bilateral ptosis and intermittent double vision on far lateral gaze remain. Speech and swallow normal, strength normal.

HIV: VL 6,200, CD4 262. ID restarted bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide.
OUD: buprenorphine/naloxone restarted and titrated back to 8/2 mg twice daily. Naloxone kit given.

Discharge medications:
1. bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 1 tab daily
2. buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 mg SL BID (bridge to PCP)
3. naloxone 4 mg nasal spray PRN

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; neurology clinic in 4-6 weeks; HIV clinic as scheduled.
No driving while double vision persists.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary and neuro consult received and routed to PCP. Spoke with pt: home since 5/7, says he feels "like I got hit by a truck" but eating normally. Eyes still droop by evening, double vision only looking far to the side. On both meds again. Not driving, a coworker is giving him rides. Hospital films last until 5/14. Booked 5/13 with PCP.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after his 4/19-5/7 admission for wound botulism (forearm injection site), records reviewed.

He's frank about it: stopped both the films and the HIV pill in March after the cravings built up, went back to using. Didn't answer our calls because he was embarrassed. Glad to be back on everything.

Now: swallowing normal, voice normal. Lids heavier at the end of the day. Double vision only at the far edge of side gaze, rare. Arms feel normal. Tired. Lost 5 kg in hospital, eating well now. No use since admission. Has naloxone.

Exam: afebrile. Mild symmetric ptosis, pupils now reactive. EOM full with a few beats of diplopia on far right gaze. Speech clear. Strength 5/5 throughout. R forearm debridement site healing, clean.
UDS bup +, otherwise negative. PDMP: only the hospital Rx.

A/P
1. Wound botulism, recovering. Neuro clinic 6/10. No driving until the double vision is fully gone.
2. OUD, relapse in March, back on buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 BID. Rx 2 weeks then visits every 2-4 wk for now. We talked about how to reach me when it starts slipping again rather than going quiet.
3. HIV, ART restarted in hospital. Will remind the HIV clinic.
4. Smoking: 1 ppd.

RTC 2 weeks (video ok), in person in June.

documents.title: Buprenorphine/naloxone refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with pt by phone, doing ok, no use, eyes better. Buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 mg films BID, #56, sent. PDMP reviewed. In-person visit 6/17.

documents.title: Neurology clinic follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology Clinic
Visit date: 06/10/2025
Re: Brandon Crowley

Follow-up after wound botulism treated with antitoxin in April. He reports his eyelids and vision are back to normal for about two weeks now, no double vision even when tired. Chewing, swallowing and speech normal. Strength normal at work.

Meds: bictegravir/FTC/TAF daily, buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 mg BID, naloxone PRN. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: lids symmetric without ptosis. Pupils equal and briskly reactive. Extraocular movements full, no diplopia in any direction including sustained gaze. Facial strength, palate and tongue normal. Strength full in all limbs including neck flexors. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Sensation intact.

Impression: full recovery from wound botulism.
Plan: no further neurology follow-up needed. Cleared to drive from a neurologic standpoint. Prevention of recurrence rests on treatment of his opioid use disorder, which he is engaged in.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Preventive visit, 33M.

Interval: septic arthritis 10/2024 and wound botulism 4/2025, both fully recovered. HIV suppressed in July per ID (VL <20, CD4 371). On buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 BID, no use since April.

No complaints. Working full time on a framing crew. Eats two meals a day, a lot of takeout. Sleeps ok.
Smokes 1 ppd (about 13 pack-years). Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month. No other drugs.
FH: father with CAD, mother with HTN, brother with depression. No new history.

Meds: bictegravir/FTC/TAF daily; buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 BID; naloxone nasal spray PRN. NKDA.

Exam: well-appearing. Vitals normal, weight back to 71 kg. HEENT normal, no thrush. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Skin: healed scar R forearm, old antecubital marks, no active sites. Joints normal. Neuro: lids symmetric, EOM full, strength normal. Mood good, PHQ-9 5, AUDIT-C 2.
UDS bup +, otherwise negative.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, hep C antibody (yearly while risk continues). Tdap today. Flu and COVID in October. Vaccines otherwise current (PCV20, hep B series, MenACWY x2).
2. HIV: per ID, suppressed.
3. OUD in early remission on buprenorphine: continue, 4-week Rx.
4. Tobacco: discussed varenicline and patches again; he'll think about it, no Rx today.

RTC 3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: HIV clinic follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Infectious Disease / HIV Clinic
Visit date: 02/11/2026
Re: Brandon Crowley

He reports missing ART for several weeks over the holidays, restarted mid-January. No new symptoms.

Meds: bictegravir/FTC/TAF daily; buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 mg BID; naloxone PRN. Allergies: NKDA.

Labs today: HIV-1 RNA 7,400 copies/mL, CD4 228 (from <20 and 371 in July).

Assessment: viremia from the adherence gap, already back on therapy for about four weeks. Bictegravir has a high barrier to resistance; no change in regimen. Adherence counseling done; pharmacy blister packs arranged. Repeat viral load in 3 months.

documents.title: Re: HIV clinic labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Brandon, I saw the HIV clinic note. The virus came back up while you were off the pills, which is what we'd expect, and it should come back down now that you're taking them every day. Let's talk about what helps you stay on track when I see you March 27.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for bup follow-up and to go over the HIV clinic visit. Using the blister packs, says he hasn't missed a dose since mid-January. No opioid use in almost a year; cravings rare. Work picking back up. No fever, cough or night sweats. Smoking a pack a day.

O: vitals normal, weight 72 kg. Well-appearing. No thrush, no nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Joints normal. Skin no new injection sites.
PHQ-9 4. UDS bup +, otherwise negative. PDMP reviewed.

A/P
1. HIV with recent viremia after a gap in ART; back on bictegravir/FTC/TAF with blister packs. ID rechecking VL in May. Reinforced.
2. OUD in early remission on buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 BID: continue, monthly refills.

reports.text: Noncontrast images followed by post-contrast images through the brain. The lateral and third ventricles are mildly enlarged, with rounding of the temporal horns. Enhancement of the basal meninges around the suprasellar cistern and brainstem on post-contrast images. No territorial infarct. No hemorrhage. No mass effect or midline shift. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Calvarium and visualized sinuses unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Mild hydrocephalus and basilar meningeal enhancement. No evidence of stroke.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Lungs clear without consolidation, nodule or cavity. No hilar or mediastinal adenopathy. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal.
Comparison 05/05/2026. Ventricular size is unchanged, mildly enlarged. No new hemorrhage or infarct. No mass effect.

documents.title: Discharge Summary: tuberculous meningitis
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Community teaching hospital, Infectious Disease service
Admitted 05/05/2026 (ICU), floor 05/13, discharged 05/29/2026

Principal diagnosis: tuberculous meningitis
Other: HIV with viremia; opioid use disorder on buprenorphine; history of IV drug use
Allergies: NKDA

Presentation: 33-year-old man with two weeks of worsening headache with fever, vomiting, light sensitivity and a stiff neck. Prior admissions for septic arthritis (2024) and wound botulism (2025). T 38.6 C, HR 102. Drowsy but oriented to person, place and time. Neck stiff with a positive Brudzinski sign. Fundi without papilledema. Cranial nerves intact; no focal neurologic deficit.

CT head: mild hydrocephalus with basilar meningeal enhancement, no stroke.
CSF: WBC 150/uL, 80% lymphocytes; protein 100 mg/dL; glucose 20 mg/dL (serum 90). Gram stain negative. AFB smear negative. TB nucleic acid amplification positive for M. tuberculosis, rifampin resistance not detected (05/06). Mycobacterial culture pending at discharge.
Chest x-ray normal. HIV-1 RNA 31,000, CD4 156.

Course: rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol with pyridoxine from 05/06. Dexamethasone IV, switched to oral and tapering over 8 weeks total. Neurosurgery reviewed the imaging; repeat CT 05/12 unchanged, no shunt needed as he improved clinically. Headache and fever resolved by the second week. ART changed because of rifampin interactions: dolutegravir 50 mg twice daily plus emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate daily. TMP-SMX DS daily added for pneumocystis prophylaxis (CD4 <200). Buprenorphine/naloxone continued 8/2 mg BID; monitor for withdrawal given rifampin.

Discharge medications:
1. rifampin 600 mg daily
2. isoniazid 300 mg daily
3. pyrazinamide 1500 mg daily
4. ethambutol 1200 mg daily
5. pyridoxine 50 mg daily
6. dexamethasone taper per schedule
7. dolutegravir 50 mg BID
8. emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 200/300 mg daily
9. TMP-SMX 800/160 mg daily
10. buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 mg SL BID
11. naloxone nasal spray PRN

Disposition: home. Directly observed therapy arranged through the local health department TB program. ID clinic in 4-6 weeks. PCP follow-up.

documents.title: Infectious disease clinic follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Infectious Disease Clinic
Visit date: 07/08/2026
Re: Brandon Crowley

Follow-up for tuberculous meningitis (culture-confirmed, fully susceptible) and HIV. Taking all doses under DOT, none missed per health department. Headache gone. No fever, vomiting or vision change. Finished the dexamethasone taper.

Exam: alert and oriented, neck supple, no meningeal signs. Cranial nerves intact. No focal deficits. Gait normal.
Labs: liver tests normal. HIV-1 RNA 140 copies/mL (from 31,000), CD4 198.

Assessment: good response. Intensive phase completed 07/07/2026.
Plan:
- Stop pyrazinamide and ethambutol. Continue rifampin 600 mg and isoniazid 300 mg daily with pyridoxine for 10 more months (12 months total for CNS disease).
- Continue dolutegravir 50 mg BID + emtricitabine/TDF while on rifampin; switch back to single-tablet regimen two weeks after rifampin ends.
- Continue TMP-SMX until CD4 above 200 on two checks.
- Monthly LFTs. Return in 6 weeks.
